why: The owner decided on 2026-11-22 that a Haxe unit of work over database/sql and Dolt-driver externs owns M09 writes, with no write through a handwritten Go island and no extern over an upstream Beads package. ADR 0008 governs over the older PRD lines that say typed Go adapters or typed facades. The island rule lets the agent delete or narrow island code without an owner question and refuses any new exported symbol, upstream import or write-capable call.

decision: Advanced the BeadsHX compiler lock to haxe.go 52a26ac8 (haxe_go-gqhg, haxe_go-l217, haxe_go-fzdf, haxe_go-almk, haxe_go-4jle, haxe_go-241z, haxe_go-15zf, haxe_go-gjqe): every Go keyword is escaped in generated names; the go.* conversion of Sys.args and Sys.command stays in the staged Sys module; locals stay off main-class static Go names; a checked cast to an abstract tests the type Haxe records; Int widens to Float through abstracts and Dynamic reads; Go lowering and type-usage tracking stop repeating whole-compile work.
why: These fixes remove compiler gaps that ports can hit, turn the compiler's master CI green again (haxe_go-241z), and make the BeadsHX compile about 18% faster (about 6.8%, 8.2% and 3.6% in paired runs for #133, #135 and #137). BeadsHX Go output changes only from haxe_go-l217: main calls Sys_args() instead of an inlined copy (3 generated files; QA ac8ee843 -> 954d9a77: build, full parity and lint pass). Every other step is byte-identical (QA on #133-#138, 0 files differ). Regenerating BeadsHX and rerunning parity and the branch gate proves the change leaves BeadsHX behavior unchanged.
